conda_environment.name: rbpbench-splits-002
conda_environment.solver: libmamba (succeeded without the classic-solver fallback needed for 001b)
conda_environment.created_with: conda create -n rbpbench-splits-002 -c conda-forge -c bioconda 'mmseqs2=18.8cc5c=h8b377d6_0' python pip -y
conda_environment.note: python resolved to the newest solver-compatible build (3.14.7) rather than 3.11, since no python version was pinned; the project's own requires-python is >=3.10 (pyproject.toml), and rbpbench==0.1.0 installs and imports cleanly under 3.14.7 (pip install -e . --no-deps).

mmseqs2.bioconda_search_confirmation: conda search -c bioconda -c conda-forge 'mmseqs2=18.8cc5c' --platform osx-64 returned exactly one match: mmseqs2 18.8cc5c h8b377d6_0 bioconda

command_distinction_confirmed_against_re.note: `mmseqs cluster --help` (18.8cc5c) does not list --search-type or --strand at all; `mmseqs search --help` lists both. This is why the frozen grouping rule binds nucleotide clustering through the explicit --dbtype 2 database instead of an unsupported cluster flag, and reserves --search-type 3 / --strand 2 for the separate audit-search workflow (see docs/tasks/002_sequence_clustered_partitions.md and src/rbpbench/splits/commands.py).

cluster_reverse_complement_fixture.fixture: row_0 (random), row_1_rc_of_row0 (true, non-palindromic reverse complement of row_0), row_2_unrelated (unrelated random sequence), row_3_identical_to_row0 (exact duplicate of row_0)
cluster_reverse_complement_fixture.result: row_0, row_1_rc_of_row0, and row_3_identical_to_row0 clustered together at every width; row_2_unrelated remained a singleton cluster at every width
cluster_reverse_complement_fixture.verified_by: tests/test_splits_real_binaries.py::RealClusteringReverseComplementFixtureTests (real binary, all three widths, all passing)

audit_search_strand_fixture.result_strand_2_both: 1 hit: q_forward vs t_rc (the target's non-palindromic reverse complement), 100% identity, 100% coverage
